docs.purpose: The map you land on when an address does not resolve to exactly one lot. Three ways to get here: the address is linked to several lots (a corner, severed or ranged property), the address exists but no lot is linked to it, or what was typed is an intersection rather than an address. In each case it is supposed to draw the lots on a map and let you tap the one you meant, and say plainly when nothing is linked rather than quietly picking the nearest polygon. Today it is a STUB: the route, the navigation and the three explanations are real, and the map is not drawn yet.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly, and today it reads no contract either — it renders from its two route parameters. The map it is specified to draw needs parcel GEOMETRY, which is exactly what `/api/parcels/lookup` does not return: the consumer parcel payload is a `.strict()` whitelist of cost menu, areas and neighbourhood, with no polygon, no centroid and no address-point id. That gap is the reason this is a stub and not a screen. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it is specified against a contract that does not exist yet, so there is nothing to re-project until the geometry is served. It renders through the LIST renderer with `render.projection: map`: a map is a projection of a collection, not an archetype, which is the same call already made for `mobile_map`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

checks.why: operator ruling 2026-09-16 (match TYPE, never count): the unlinked case must render a VISIBLE "no lot is linked to this address" state. Picking the nearest polygon and presenting it as the answer is explicitly forbidden, and it is the kind of thing that is invisible once shipped — hence blocking, not advisory. The paired lock upstream is mobile/__tests__/parcelSearchMatch.test.ts, which asserts a zero-candidate response derives `no_match` and never `unlinked`.

While this surface is a stub it must SAY it is a stub. The permanently non-zero condition is the stub itself; the retighten condition is machine-observable — the check flips to FAIL the day the route renders a MapView, because at that point an explanatory placeholder is a defect rather than an honest state.

deviations.why: Registered as `status: exists` while being a STUB. The route, the navigation contract and the three explanations are real and in the tree; the `map` projection is not drawn. Recorded as a deviation rather than carrying `status: designed`, because `designed` would claim nothing is built and something is — and the alternative, leaving the three map outcomes to dead-end silently on the SEARCH surface, is worse than a stub that says so.

limitations.measured: src/app/api/admin/parcels/lookup/types.ts:123 — matchType is [exact|typeahead|direct]; mobile/src/lib/parcelSearchMatch.ts:98-123 derives only unique / text_candidates / intersection / no_match.

notes: Created by operator ruling 2026-09-16 (match TYPE, never count), which separated the map disambiguation from the SEARCH surface on the grounds that it reads parcel geometry and S-002 does not. Archetype is LIST, not a new "MAP" archetype, because Spec 126 §3.1 defines a map as a `render.projection` — the same call already made for `mobile_map`. This is the next surface to build; it is blocked on the API change recorded in S-002’s limitations.
